title_ar: بيان من العلامة الددو حول جريمة تمزيق المصحف الشريف
title_en: A Statement from the Learned al-Dedew on the Crime of Tearing Up the Noble Qur'an
body_ar:
أصدر العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو الشنقيطي رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء اليوم الثلاثاء 3ربيع الثاني 1435هـ، الموافق 4 مارس 2014م، بيانا حول جريمة تمزيق المصحف الشريف، قال فيه: " إن على الجميع حكاما و محكومين أن يضجوا إلى الله بإنكار هذا المنكر مشددا على ضرورة البحث عن الجناة حتى تنزل بهم أقسى العقوبات و ينفذ حكم الله فيهم حاثا العلماء على القيام بالقسط و أن يبلغوا رسالة الله تعالى و أن لا تأخذهم في الحق لومة لائم مؤكدا على ضرورة إنكار هذا المنكر من عموم الشعب و أن يحافظوا على أمن الأرواح و الأموال و أن يتقيدوا بالضوابط و الآداب الشريعة، مضيفا " يجب على رجال الأمن أن لا يتعرضوا للمتظاهرين السلميين فمهمتهم حفظ الأمن لا إثارة الفوضى و حفظ الأنفس لا إزهاقها. و السلاح المشترى بمال الشعب لا يحل أن يستغل لقتل الشعب و إذلاله من غير سبب." داعيا وسائل الاعلام أن تلتزم الصدق و العدل و أن لا تكون مصدرا للتحريض و الفساد مبينا على ضرورة معرفة الجميع أن التعامل مع هذا النوع من الجرائم لا يكون مطلقا بالتجاهل و التشكيك محذرا من الأيادي الخفية لأعداء كتب الله المنزلة من اليهود و أعوانهم حاثا الجميع أن تكون هذه الأحداث الجسيمة مصدرا لوحدة الصف و اجتماع الكلمة و تقارب وجهات النظر فلا خلاف في إنكارها بين الجميع.

و هذا نص البيان : 

الحمد لله على كل حال و نعوذ بالله من حال أهل النار ، أما بعد فقد صدمت ـ كما صدم غيري ـ من تمزيق كتاب الله في بيت الله ، و زاد الصدمة ما تناقله الناس من أن مقترف الجريمة ليس فردا يمكن أن يكون مختل العقل ، بل عصابة تآمرت على هذه الجريمة النكراء و أبرمتها بليل، فذكر قول الله تعالى: " كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاهَا * إِذِ انْبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا * فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ نَاقَةَ اللَّهِ وَسُقْيَاهَا * فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاهَا * فَلا يَخَافُ عُقْبَاهَا " وكانت الجريمة في عاصمة الجمهورية الاسلامية الموريتانية ، فأردت بيان ما يلي :

1- يجب على الجميع حكاما و محكومين أن يضجوا الى الله بإنكار هذا المنكر الشنيع. الذي تكاد السموات يتفطرن منه و تنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا و البراءة إلى الله منه ومن مقترفيه ، و أن يحتجوا بكل الوسائل المشروعة

2- يجب على أولياء الأمر –وفقهم الله- أن يبحثوا عن الجناة حتى ينزلوا بهم أقسى العقوبات و ينفذوا فيهم حكم الله الذي قال جل من قائل : " إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم " 

3- يجب على العلماء أن يقوموا بالقسط و أن يبلغوا رسالات الله و أن لا تأخذهم في الله لومة لائم، و أن يفعلوا ما فعل الامام مالك بن أنس رحمه الله حين أراد حاكم المدينة تعطيل حد الذي قتل أخاه غيلة، فقال مالك و الله لا أتكلم في العلم حتى يقتل، فأضرب عن العمل فماجت المدينة حتى قتل.

4- يجب على عموم الشعب أن يكون إنكارهم للمنكر بالمعروف و أن لا يعتدوا، و أن يحافظوا على أمن الأرواح و الأموال و أن يتقيدوا بالضوابط و الآداب الشريعة.

5- يجب على رجال الأمن أن لا يتعرضوا للمتظاهرين السلميين فمهمتهم حفظ الأمن لا إثارة الفوضى و حفظ الأنفس لا إزهاقها. و السلاح المشترى بمال الشعب لا يحل أن يستغل لقتل الشعب و إذلاله من غير سبب.

6ـ يجب على وسائل الاعلام الرسمية و الحرة أن تلتزم الصدق و العدل و أن لا تكون وسيلة للتحريض و الإفساد.

7- يجب أن يعلم الجميع أن التعامل مع هذا النوع من الجرائم لا يكون بالتجاهل أو التشكيك و كذلك احتمال أن تكون المصاحف من قبل، أو أن تكون الدواجن هي التي مزقتها، فلمصلحة من تذكر هذه الاحتمالات البعيدة .

8- يجب أن يخاف الجميع أن تكون أيدي اليهود و من هاد إليهم من وراء هذا المنكر فهم أعداء كتب الله المنزلة ، كما قال تعالى : " مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّلَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِّلْكَافِرِينَ وَلَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ ۖ وَمَا يَكْفُرُ بِهَا إِلَّا الْفَاسِقُونَ أَوَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُوا عَهْدًا نَّبَذَهُ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُم ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ مِّنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ " 

9- يجب أن تكون هذه الأحداث الجسيمة داعية لوحدة الصف و اجتماع الكلمة و تقارب و جهات النظر، فلا خلاف في إنكارها بين الجميع.

و أسأل الله الكريم أن يجنب بلادنا الفتن و الفساد و أن يقمع أهل الزيغ و العناد و أن يؤلف بين قلوبنا و يصلح ذات بيننا و أن لا يؤاخذنا بما فعل السفهاء منا و صلى الله وسلم على بينا محمد و على ءاله و صحبه .

كتبه محمد الحسن الددو
body_en:
The learned Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew al-Shinqiti, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, issued today, Tuesday 3 Rabiʿ al-Thani 1435 AH, corresponding to 4 March 2014, a statement on the crime of tearing up the noble Qur'an, in which he said: "It is incumbent upon everyone, rulers and ruled, to cry out to God in denunciation of this wrong", stressing the necessity of searching for the perpetrators until the harshest punishments are brought down upon them and God's ruling is carried out upon them; urging the scholars to uphold justice, and to convey the message of God the Exalted, and not to let the blame of any blamer deter them in the truth; affirming the necessity that the general body of the people denounce this wrong, and that they preserve the safety of lives and property, and that they abide by the constraints and the proprieties of the Sharia; adding: "The men of the security forces must not confront peaceful demonstrators, for their task is the keeping of security, not the stirring up of disorder, and the preservation of lives, not the taking of them. And weapons bought with the people's money may not lawfully be used to kill the people and to humiliate them without cause"; calling upon the media to hold to truthfulness and justice and not to be a source of incitement and corruption; making clear the necessity that everyone know that dealing with this kind of crime is never by ignoring it and by casting doubt on it; warning against the hidden hands of the enemies of the books God has sent down, from among the Jews and their helpers; urging everyone that these grave events should be a source of unity of ranks, of coming together, and of the drawing near of points of view, for there is no disagreement among anyone in denouncing them.

And this is the text of the statement:

Praise be to God in every state, and we seek refuge in God from the state of the people of the Fire. To proceed: I was shocked — as others were shocked — by the tearing up of the Book of God in the House of God; and what increased the shock was what people have passed on, that the perpetrator of the crime is not an individual who might be of unsound mind, but a gang that conspired to this abominable crime and settled it by night. So there was recalled the saying of God the Exalted: {Thamud denied in their insolence, when the most wretched of them was sent forth; and the Messenger of God said to them: the she-camel of God, and her drink! But they denied him and hamstrung her, so their Lord crushed them for their sin and levelled it; and He does not fear its outcome} (Sūrat al-Shams 91:11–15). And the crime took place in the capital of the Islamic Republic of Mauritania. So I wished to make clear the following:

1 – It is obligatory (wājib) upon everyone, rulers and ruled, to cry out to God in denunciation of this hideous wrong — at which the heavens are near to splitting apart, and the earth to cleaving, and the mountains to falling down in ruin — and to declare before God their innocence of it and of those who perpetrated it; and to protest by every lawful means.

2 – It is obligatory upon those in authority — may God grant them success — to search out the perpetrators until they bring down upon them the harshest punishments and carry out upon them the ruling of God, who said, majestic is He who speaks: {The recompense of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the earth is only that they be killed, or crucified, or that their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides, or that they be banished from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:33).

3 – It is obligatory upon the scholars to uphold justice, and to convey the messages of God, and not to let the blame of any blamer deter them in God; and to do as Imam Malik ibn Anas, may God have mercy on him, did when the governor of Medina wanted to suspend the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) upon the man who had killed his brother by stealth. Malik said: by God, I will not speak on knowledge until he is killed; and he withheld from his work, so that Medina was thrown into turmoil until the man was killed.

4 – It is obligatory upon the general body of the people that their denunciation of wrong be by what is right, and that they not transgress; and that they preserve the safety of lives and property, and that they abide by the constraints and the proprieties of the Sharia.

5 – It is obligatory upon the men of the security forces not to confront peaceful demonstrators, for their task is the keeping of security, not the stirring up of disorder, and the preservation of lives, not the taking of them. And weapons bought with the people's money may not lawfully be used to kill the people and to humiliate them without cause.

6 – It is obligatory upon the media, official and free, to hold to truthfulness and justice, and not to be a means of incitement and of corruption.

7 – Everyone must know that dealing with this kind of crime is not by ignoring it or by casting doubt on it — nor likewise by the possibility that the copies of the Qur'an were [torn] beforehand, or that it was poultry that tore them. For whose benefit are these far-fetched possibilities brought up?

8 – Everyone must fear that the hands of the Jews, and of those who side with them, are behind this wrong; for they are the enemies of the books God has sent down, as God the Exalted said: {Whoever is an enemy to God, and His angels, and His messengers, and Gabriel and Michael — then indeed God is an enemy to the disbelievers. And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, and none denies them except the defiantly disobedient. Is it not so that every time they made a covenant, a party of them cast it aside? Rather, most of them do not believe. And when a messenger came to them from God, confirming what was with them, a party of those who had been given the Scripture cast the Book of God behind their backs, as though they did not know} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:98–101).

9 – These grave events must be a summons to unity of ranks, to coming together, and to the drawing near of points of view, for there is no disagreement among anyone in denouncing them.

And I ask God, the Generous, to spare our land trials and corruption, and to subdue the people of deviation and obstinacy, and to bring our hearts together, and to set right the relations between us, and not to take us to task for what the foolish among us have done. And may God bless and grant peace to our Prophet Muhammad, and his family and his Companions.

Written by Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew

flags.arabic: 8- يجب أن يخاف الجميع أن تكون أيدي اليهود و من هاد إليهم من وراء هذا المنكر فهم أعداء كتب الله المنزلة
flags.context: point 8 of the statement, and the corresponding clause in the site's summary
options: Everyone must fear that the hands of the Jews, and of those who side with them, are behind this wrong
Everyone must be apprehensive that Jewish hands and their allies lie behind this wrong
Everyone must beware that the hands of the Jews and those who incline to them are behind this wrong
flags.note: EDITORIAL — THE HIGHEST-EXPOSURE PASSAGE IN THIS ENTIRE SLICE, AND IT MUST NOT BE PUBLISHED WITHOUT A DECISION TAKEN AT THE LEVEL OF UMMAH COLLECTIVE AND THE SHEIKH'S OFFICE. Point 8 attributes responsibility for an unsolved crime in Nouakchott to 'the hands of the Jews', as a collective, and supports it with a Qur'anic passage about the People of the Scripture. In English this is an antisemitic conspiracy claim about a contemporary criminal act. It is actionable or prosecutable under the incitement, hate-speech and public-order laws of several Western jurisdictions, it would breach the content policies of every major platform, and it carries severe reputational consequences for any body publishing it. Style guide section 6 forbids softening, so it has NOT been softened, paraphrased or abridged: the translation says what the Arabic says. Section 12 places the publication decision with Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, never with the translator and never by default. My recommendation as translator is that this record be withheld from publication in its entirety pending that decision — not merely that point 8 be excerpted away, since removing one numbered point from a nine-point signed statement would itself misrepresent the document. من هاد إليهم is literally 'those who incline towards them'; there is also a play on هاد / يهود.

flags.arabic: 2- … حتى ينزلوا بهم أقسى العقوبات و ينفذوا فيهم حكم الله … " إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله … أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض "
options: reproduce the demand and the verse in full, as the statement has them
summarise the point
flags.note: EDITORIAL, second highest exposure. A public demand that the state inflict 'the harshest punishments' on named suspects in an ongoing criminal matter, evidenced by the ḥirābah verse, which specifies killing, crucifixion, cross-amputation and banishment. In English this reads as a call for corporal and capital punishment against identified individuals, published before any trial. The Sheikh does not himself say which of the verse's punishments should be applied, and the English must not be allowed to imply that he specified one; nor may the verse be trimmed. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

flags.arabic: فذكر قول الله تعالى: " كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاهَا …"
options: so there was recalled the saying of God the Exalted (reading فذُكِّر, passive)
so he recalled the saying of God the Exalted
so [I] was reminded of the saying of God the Exalted
flags.note: GRAMMATICAL AMBIGUITY, unresolved. The statement is in the first person throughout ('I was shocked', 'I wished to make clear'), but فذكر is unpointed and may be read as passive (one was reminded), as active third person, or as a slip for فذكرت ('I recalled'). A passive rendering has been used because it commits least; a reviewer should decide. Note also that invoking Sūrat al-Shams, on the destruction of Thamud for hamstringing the she-camel, places the perpetrators under a Qur'anic type of those annihilated for a collective crime — which is part of why point 2 reads as it does, and should be visible to a reader.

flags.arabic: قال فيه: " إن على الجميع … مضيفا " يجب على رجال الأمن … من غير سبب."
flags.context: the quotation marks in the site's opening summary paragraph
options: reproduce the quotation marks as the source places them and flag
close the first quotation where the reported speech appears to end
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). The summary opens a quotation at 'It is incumbent upon everyone' and never closes it; a second quotation is then opened at 'The men of the security forces' and is closed. As printed, there is no way to tell where the Sheikh's quoted words end and the site's reporting-verb chain ('stressing…', 'urging…', 'affirming…') begins. The English reproduces the defect. The matching sentences in the statement itself, which follows, are the reliable text and should be preferred for any quotation.

flags.arabic: و كذلك احتمال أن تكون المصاحف من قبل، أو أن تكون الدواجن هي التي مزقتها
options: the possibility that the copies of the Qur'an were [torn] beforehand, or that it was poultry that tore them
the possibility that the copies were already [damaged], or that chickens tore them
reproduce the clause with the lacuna visible
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): أن تكون المصاحف من قبل has no predicate — a participle such as ممزقة ('already torn') has dropped out, and the sense must be supplied from the parallel clause. The English marks the supplied word in brackets rather than writing it in. The reference to poultry is not an error: it is the Sheikh rejecting explanations that were being put about locally at the time, and the sarcasm of the following question ('for whose benefit are these far-fetched possibilities brought up?') is his.

flags.arabic: ما فعل الامام مالك بن أنس … حين أراد حاكم المدينة تعطيل حد الذي قتل أخاه غيلة … فأضرب عن العمل فماجت المدينة حتى قتل
options: he withheld from his work (i.e. from teaching and giving fatwa)
he went on strike from work
he abstained from acting
flags.note: EDITORIAL and lexical. The example held up to the scholars is Malik's refusal to teach until a killer was executed, which brought public pressure to bear on the governor — that is, a scholar using his authority to force the state's hand on a capital case. That is the point of the analogy and it must not be blunted. أضرب عن العمل in modern Arabic is 'went on strike'; the rendering 'withheld from his work' avoids an anachronistic register while keeping the sense. حدّ is the prescribed Sharia punishment and is not in the glossary; a candidate for addition. غيلة is killing by stealth or treachery, a category that in Maliki law removes the heirs' option to pardon — which is exactly why suspending the punishment was contentious.

flags.arabic: يجب على أولياء الأمر … يجب على العلماء … يجب على عموم الشعب … يجب على رجال الأمن … يجب على وسائل الاعلام
options: render every يجب as 'it is obligatory (wājib)', as the fixed mapping requires
vary it as 'must' or 'should' for readability
flags.note: RULING WORDS. Every one of the nine points is built on يجب, and the fixed mapping has been applied without variation, including where an English writer would naturally have varied it. This matters because the points address different parties — the state, the scholars, the public, the security forces, the media — and the document's force is that it places the SAME obligation on all of them. Note that point 5 uses لا يحل ('is not lawful'), a different formulation, and the English marks that difference.

flags.arabic: الذي تكاد السموات يتفطرن منه و تنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا … و صلى الله وسلم على بينا محمد و على ءاله
options: translate by the evident sense and record the defects
correct the source
flags.note: SOURCE, recorded not corrected (house rule 11). (1) The wording in point 1 is that of Sūrat Maryam 19:90, woven unmarked into the Sheikh's own sentence, with no quotation marks and no citation; none has been added, and it has not been set in the Qur'anic braces. (2) The closing has بينا for نبينا ('our Prophet'), a dropped nūn. (3) ءاله is the source's spelling of آله. (4) '6ـ' uses a taṭwīl instead of a hyphen, unlike the other eight points. (5) الاعلام and الامر appear without hamzah. None affects the sense.

flags.context: the date in the site's opening sentence
options: reproduce both dates as printed
expand and verify the conversion
flags.note: The two dates are consistent and the CMS timestamp of the same day agrees with them, so for once the date is probably the real date of composition rather than a bulk-upload artefact. date_is_cms_upload is nonetheless left true, because the CMS field is still a CMS field and the corpus-wide rule should not be varied per record on an inference.

flags.context: the CMS timestamp on the record
options: treat as the date the item was uploaded to the CMS
treat as the date of composition
flags.note: CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT. The CMS serves a bulk-upload timestamp, not the date the Sheikh spoke or wrote. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Where the body itself names a date, that internal date is the better evidence and is kept in the English.

translator_notes: RECOMMENDATION: withhold this record from publication pending an editorial decision. See the flag on point 8. The file is complete and faithful; the question is not translation but publication.

Two texts in one record: the site's summary paragraph, then 'And this is the text of the statement', then the signed statement itself. The two say the same things in different words, and only the second is the Sheikh's own. Where they differ, the statement governs.

Typed 'article' rather than 'fatwa': it is a public statement (bayān) on a current event, signed by the Sheikh, not an answer to a question. The CMS files it under 'news', which is recorded in section but does not fit a signed statement by the Sheikh himself.

المنكر is rendered 'wrong' throughout, consistently with the glossary's 'forbidding wrong' (al-nahy ʿan al-munkar), and إنكار as 'denunciation'; the document is an exercise of that duty and the vocabulary should be visibly the same.

أولياء الأمر is rendered 'those in authority'; in this document it plainly means the Mauritanian state authorities, not the scholars — unlike record 860, where the same Qur'anic phrase (أولو الأمر) is reported as taken of the scholars. The two renderings differ deliberately and should not be harmonised.

The two Qur'anic passages are printed in the source between ordinary quotation marks, with the Uthmani orthography and its pause marks; body_ar preserves them exactly, and body_en uses the curly braces required by style guide section 4. The source page carried two external reference links, to library.islamweb.net (a tafsir) and to quran.ksu.edu.sa (Ibn Kathir on Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:101), neither of which has visible anchor text in the served body.

The events referred to are the tearing of copies of the Qur'an in a mosque in Nouakchott in early March 2014, and the protests that followed. No background has been added to the English beyond what the document itself says.
dec: Attributes responsibility for an unsolved crime to ‘the hands of the Jews’ as a collective. Prosecutable under the incitement provisions of several European states.
